title: Directly and efficiently optimizing prediction error and AUC of linear classifiers
contribution: Under Gaussian class distributions the expected 0-1 error and AUC of a linear classifier are smooth with closed-form gradients in the first two moments, so they can be optimized directly with per-iteration cost independent of n (Thms 2-7, pp. 4-5; p. 8).
problem_entry: Surrogate losses are used only because empirical 0-1 error and AUC have zero or undefined gradients; pairwise AUC surrogates are also expensive (abstract p. 1; pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Replace the surrogate by the expected metric in closed form via Gaussianity of w^T X, with empirical moments computed once; keep plain GD with Armijo backtracking (Thms 2, 6, pp. 4-5; Alg. 1 p. 5).
assumptions: Gaussian class-conditional (or joint) distributions; the authors argue near-normality of w^T X by a dependent-variable CLT and leave theory to future work (pp. 4-5).
proof_devices: closure of Gaussians under linear maps (Tong) giving F_error = P(+)(1-phi(mu+/sigma+)) + P(-)phi(mu-/sigma-) (Thm 2, p. 4)
chain rule for phi(w^T mu / sqrt(w^T Sigma w)) (Lemma 2, p. 4)
experiments: 9 synthetic Gaussian sets (exact vs empirical moments vs logistic/pairwise hinge) and 19 LIBSVM/UCI sets, 20 runs each; accuracy/AUC and time; losing cases' traces shown; LDA in appendix (pp. 6-8, 12-13).
positioning: Positions against surrogate ERM (logistic, hinge, pairwise losses) and against LDA as the classical Gaussian-assumption method (p. 2, p. 5).
writing: Advantage stated as data-size-independent iterations; failures reported with a one-line cause hypothesis and deferred to future work (p. 2, p. 7).
limits_future: Gaussian assumption not justified theoretically; stalls on 2 data sets; future: second-order methods (p. 5, p. 7, p. 8).

title: New convergence aspects of stochastic gradient algorithms
contribution: Convergence of SGD and Hogwild! (a.s. and O(1/t) in expectation) for strongly convex F without the bounded-gradient assumption, by deriving the second-moment bound from per-realization smoothness, plus a larger admissible class of diminishing step sizes (pp. 4-5, 6-8, 14-16).
problem_entry: The classical bound E||grad f||^2 <= sigma^2 contradicts strong convexity (shown on p. 3); Bottou et al.'s M,N bound has unknown constants (p. 3).
key_idea: Keep SGD/Hogwild! and derive E||grad f(w;xi)||^2 <= 4L[F(w)-F*] + N from per-sample L-smoothness (+convexity), giving explicit constants and larger initial steps; unify Hogwild! variants by a filtered recursion (Lemma 1 p. 6; Remark 1 p. 8; pp. 9-10).
assumptions: F mu-strongly convex; every f(.;xi) L-smooth, optionally convex; i.i.d. samples; bounded delay tau with atomic coordinate reads/writes for Hogwild! (pp. 2, 6, 11).
proof_devices: ||a||^2 <= 2||a-b||^2 + 2||b||^2 with E||grad f(w;xi)-grad f(w*;xi)||^2 <= 2L[F(w)-F*] (Lemma 1 proof, pp. 21-22)
Bertsekas supermartingale convergence lemma for a.s. convergence (Lemma 5 p. 21; Thm 1 p. 7)
ODE-style comparison C(t)=e^{-M(t)} int e^{M(x)} n(x)^2 dx crossing n(t) once (Lemma 3, pp. 15-16)
experiments: l2-logistic regression on ijcnn1 and covtype, single-core simulation of the Hogwild! recursion, 10 runs, varying support fraction and delay tau in {1,10,100} (pp. 17-18).
positioning: Corrects the classical bounded-gradient analyses and sharpens Bottou-Curtis-Nocedal and Moulines-Bach (larger step class); contrasts with fixed-step Hogwild! analyses (Leblond et al.) (pp. 3-4, 8-9).
writing: Opens with a contradiction and a two-function counterexample before the contribution list; contributions as nested bullets (pp. 3-5).
limits_future: Strong convexity of F required throughout; conclusion lists no limitations or future directions (p. 2, p. 18).

title: A stochastic trust region algorithm based on careful step normalization
contribution: TRish, an SG method that takes normalized (trust-region) steps only when the stochastic gradient norm lies in an interval, with SG-type guarantees under PL and nonconvex settings and better empirical performance than tuned SG (pp. 4, 9-16, 18-23).
problem_entry: SG stepsizes have no natural scaling and must be problem dependent; always-normalized steps need strong assumptions; stochastic TR methods need random fully linear models (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Use the linear-model TR step -alpha g/||g|| only for ||g|| in [1/gamma1, 1/gamma2], SG steps outside, accept every step; safeguard motivated by an example where normalized unbiased steps ascend in expectation (Alg. p. 4; Example 2.1 p. 4).
assumptions: L-smooth bounded-below f; unbiased g with E||g||^2 <= M1 + M2||grad f||^2; optional PL; variance proportional to alpha_k^2 (batch |S_k| = alpha_k^-2) or geometrically decreasing for stronger rates (pp. 5-7, 12, 14).
proof_devices: three-case split plus event E_k={grad f^T g >= 0} isolating the normalization cost in one term (gamma1-gamma2) alpha P[E]E[grad f^T g|E] (Lemma 3.1, pp. 6-7)
bound P[E]E[grad f^T g|E] <= h1 + h2||grad f||^2 (Lemma 3.2, p. 8; referee-suggested proof, p. 24)
couple gamma1-gamma2 proportional to alpha_k to recover SG O(1/k) (Thm 3.2, p. 11)
experiments: Logistic regression (a1a, w1a, rcv1) and CNNs (mnist, cifar-10) vs SG with equal tuning budget over the same effective stepsize range, 10 runs, branch frequencies reported (pp. 18-23).
positioning: Modification of SG, contrasted with always-normalized methods ([12]) and with random-model stochastic trust region ([16],[5]) that use ratio tests and fully linear models (pp. 2-3).
writing: Hedged claims ('we contend', 'one can argue'); a worked counterexample precedes the analysis; explicit parameter-selection section linking theory to practice (pp. 2, 4, 17-18, 23).
limits_future: Only reduces stepsize problem-dependence; parameter choice needs a variance estimate; needs a larger study with stepsize decay; future: Hessian approximations, acceleration, momentum (pp. 2, 18, 23).

title: A novel smoothed loss and penalty function for noncrossing composite quantile estimation via deep neural networks
contribution: SPNN: a neural network trained on a logistic-smoothed pinball loss over multiple quantiles with a squared-hinge non-crossing penalty, applied to GEFCom2014 wind-power probabilistic forecasting (pp. 5-6, 7-9).
problem_entry: Application: multiple-quantile estimation in NNs suffers quantile crossover; reordering heuristics lack foundation and constrained SVQR is expensive (p. 1, p. 3).
key_idea: Smooth the pinball loss as tau u + alpha log(1+exp(-u/alpha)) so gradient methods apply, and add c*sum max(0, eps - (q_m - q_{m-1}))^2 to prevent crossing (eqs. 3, 5, 6, pp. 5-6).
assumptions: No theory; hyperparameters chosen empirically on training data (smoothing 0.01, penalty 1000, margin 0); activation stated as tanh (p. 5) but ReLU in case studies (p. 7).
experiments: GEFCom2014 wind, 10 zones, 2013 test year with 12-month sliding-window retraining; baselines persistence, climatology, uniform, QR, SVQR; QS, IS, ACE, sharpness, QVSS; compared with competition winners (pp. 7-9).
positioning: Extends Zheng's smooth quantile regression to NNs; contrasts with Huber-smoothed QRNN and monotone composite QRNN (pp. 5-6).
writing: Numbered contribution list in the introduction; 'we are the first' claim hedged by 'Based on our knowledge' (pp. 1-2, p. 5).
limits_future: Future: solar, wave, prices, load; very short-term forecasting from past power only; no count of crossing violations reported in results read (p. 10; pp. 6-9).

title: Novel and efficient approximations for zero-one loss of linear classifiers
contribution: Smooth closed-form approximations of expected 0-1 error and ranking loss for linear classifiers, derived by assuming only that w^T X (not X) is near-normal, optimized with L-BFGS at cost independent of n (pp. 5-7, 10, 15).
problem_entry: Same as S078: surrogates are optimized only because empirical error/ranking loss are step functions; pairwise ranking surrogates are superlinear in n (pp. 1-4).
key_idea: Move the Gaussian assumption to the 1-D projection w^T X (CLT argument), derive F_n01 and F_nrank with gradients, handle scale invariance by a (1-||w||^2)^2 penalty, and optimize with L-BFGS (pp. 5-7, 10).
assumptions: w^T X approximately normal for the w met in training; cross-covariances set to zero; objective undefined at w=0 and nonconvex (pp. 2, 5, 7-9).
proof_devices: Gaussian closure plus chain rule (Lemma 3.4, pp. 5-6)
CLT for sums of weakly dependent features as motivation (p. 5)
experiments: Histograms of projections at early/late iterates; 9 synthetic and 21 LIBSVM/UCI sets up to real-sim; accuracy/AUC, iterations, solve and moment time; LDA and ADAM baselines; objective-vs-true-loss plots along the optimization path (pp. 8-15).
positioning: Against surrogate ERM (logistic, pairwise hinge, sigmoid-smoothed ranking) and LDA; claims milder assumption than LDA's Gaussian data (pp. 2-4, 14).
writing: Argues the assumption's mildness up front and supports it by plots; conclusion claims 'theoretical motivation' rather than proof (p. 2, p. 15).
limits_future: Conclusion lists no limits; tables show covtype failure (0.5502 vs 0.7562) and LDA at or above F_n01 on several sets despite 'clearly inferior' in the text; synthetic tables identical to S078 incl. times (pp. 13-15; pp. 11-12).

title: Feature engineering and forecasting via derivative-free optimization and ensemble of sequence-to-sequence networks with applications in renewable energy
contribution: An ensemble of seq2seq LSTM networks with additive resampling, designed and tuned (hyperparameters, ensemble size, feature subset) by a scaled trust-region DFO that handles box and integer variables, tested on wind, solar and wave data (pp. 2-8, 9-19).
problem_entry: Application: multistep renewable forecasting where existing ML ignores temporal structure and seasonality; DFO as a tuner for expensive black boxes (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: SDFO-TR = DFO-TR plus an upper-bound-plus-penalty for box violations, [0,1] scaling, and piecewise-constant encoding of integer variables, used to choose hyperparameters, ensemble factor and features (p. 8, p. 14).
assumptions: Black-box loss bounded above (MAAPE <= pi/2); no smoothness claimed for the piecewise-constant objective; heuristic appeal that DFO escapes flat minima (pp. 8-9).
experiments: NREL, GECAD, NSRDB, NOAA data; 60/20/20 split; horizons 1-72; baselines ELM, SVR, RF, SARIMA, FOS-ELM, Spearmint BO; MAAPE, NRMSE, MAE; feature-selection comparison with Spearmint per metric (pp. 9-19).
positioning: Positions DFO against Bayesian optimization as time-efficient and accurate but continuous-only, and seq2seq ensembles against SVR/ELM/RF (pp. 2, 4, 9-10).
writing: Bullet-list observations after each table; strong superiority claims, with the data cut to ten days acknowledged later (pp. 11-15).
limits_future: Many features may hurt DFO; data limited by computation; future: DFO as a decision maker for parallel-structure design in other ML areas (p. 14, p. 15, p. 20).

title: Inexact SARAH algorithm for stochastic optimization
contribution: iSARAH replaces SARAH's exact outer gradient with a mini-batch of chosen size b, extending SARAH to expectation minimization with total sample complexity O(max{sigma*^2/eps, kappa} log(1/eps)) in the strongly convex case and the best known rate in the convex case under an outer-iterate assumption (pp. 4-5, 16-19).
problem_entry: SVRG/SARAH need exact gradients each outer loop, so they apply only to finite sums; SCSG applies to expectations but with worse kappa dependence (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Keep SARAH's recursive estimator and replace only the anchor gradient by a b-sample average, with b chosen to recover SARAH's rate (pp. 3-5).
assumptions: Per-sample L-smooth; strongly convex F or convex realizations as needed; E||grad f(w*;xi)||^2 <= sigma*^2; for convex multi-loop, F - F* <= M||grad F||^2 + N at outer iterates only (pp. 6-7, 17-18).
proof_devices: telescoping identity for E||grad F(w_t) - v_t||^2 from E[v_j - v_{j-1}|F_j] = grad F(w_j) - grad F(w_{j-1}) (Lemma 7, p. 10)
outer-loop linear contraction to a b-dependent floor (Thm 3, p. 16)
parameter choice eta=2/(5L), m=20kappa-1, b=max{20kappa-10, 20sigma*^2/eps} (Cor. 4, p. 17)
positioning: Compared with SVRG, SARAH, SCSG, SPIDER/SpiderBoost and ProxSARAH via complexity tables; notes an unstated assumption in original SARAH (pp. 2-4).
writing: Complexity tables with an explicit additional-assumption column; assumptions argued 'reasonable' with a constructed example (p. 4, pp. 17-19).
limits_future: One-loop needs learning rate O(eps), 'practically undesirable'; best convex rate only under Assumption 5; nonconvex bounded-variance case deferred to ProxSARAH (p. 3, p. 19).

title: Nesterov accelerated shuffling gradient method for convex optimization
contribution: NASG applies Nesterov extrapolation once per epoch of a shuffling gradient method and proves O(1/T) in epochs for convex finite sums, deterministically for any permutation and for the last iterate, improving the variance term by n for randomized shuffling (pp. 4-6).
problem_entry: Stochastic NAG has no provable acceleration without vanishing variance; shuffling SGD's best convex rate is O(1/T^{2/3}); per-iteration momentum accumulates errors (pp. 1-3).
key_idea: Keep NAG's extrapolation and shuffling SGD's inner loop but move the momentum update to epoch level, viewing the epoch as NAG with the full gradient replaced by sequential component gradients (pp. 3-4).
assumptions: Component L-smoothness; convex components (variance at optimum) or convex F with generalized bounded variance; no bounded domain/gradient; horizon-dependent step eta_t = k alpha^t/(LT) (pp. 4-5).
proof_devices: Nesterov auxiliary sequences theta^(t)=2/(t+2), v^(t) with convex-combination identities (eqs. 7-8, p. 5)
weighted key estimate with T(T+2) factor (Lemma A.1, p. 14)
experiments: Logistic regression (w8a, ijcnn1, covtype) and linear/one-hidden-layer nets on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10; baselines NAG, NASG-PI, SGD, SGD-M, Adam with random reshuffling; grid-tuned constant LR; 10 seeds; effective data passes on x-axis (pp. 7-9, 29).
positioning: Improves shuffling SGD rates (Mishchenko et al., Nguyen et al.); distinguishes from variance reduction (needs full gradients) and from per-iteration stochastic momentum (pp. 2-3).
writing: Central question posed explicitly in the introduction; complexity table with footnotes on assumption differences; remark stating guarantee type (pp. 2-3, 6).
limits_future: Open: better dependence on n; nonconvex analysis; rate is O(1/T), not NAG's O(1/T^2) (p. 9; p. 2 vs p. 5).
